s: Our phones are part of every day.
My day starts with my phone.
Every night I charge my phone next to my bed.
If I do not charge my phone at night, the battery is dead in the morning.
A dead phone is a bad start to the day.
So I always charge my phone, and then I check the screen.
The screen is the first thing we see in the morning.
Is your phone screen too bright at night?
Yes, a bright screen hurts my eyes.
So I make the screen darker before I sleep.
My screen is always too bright.
After breakfast, I open my favorite app.
I check the weather on the app every day.
Every morning I open the same weather app.
The app tells me if I need an umbrella.
I have an app for money, an app for maps, and an app for music.
What is your favorite app, Lena?
My favorite app is a cooking app.
I download new recipes from the app every week.
Last week I downloaded three new songs.
When you download a movie, do you watch it on your phone screen?
The big screen in the living room is nice, but the small screen is fine for a short trip.
Speaking of trips, I always charge my phone before I travel.
And I download a movie for the train.
I also charge my phone at the office.
I have a cable at my desk.
Do you remember all your passwords?
I have one password for my email and one password for my bank app.
I write my password in a small secret book.
A good password is long and secret.
My password keeps my photos safe.
I change my password every month.
My grandmother just got her first phone.
I teach her how to charge it every day.
Does she know how to download an app?
Last week I helped her download a photo app.
Now she can see pictures of the family on her screen.
A photo app is perfect for her.
The screen shows big happy faces.
But she is scared of the password.
She says, why does every app need a password?
Many older people feel the same.
I told my uncle to charge his phone in the car, because the car has a charger.
My uncle forgets to charge his phone too.
Then his screen goes black in the middle of a call.
A black screen and no sound.
You cannot call, you cannot download anything, and you cannot open any app.
So the first lesson is simple.
Learn one app at a time.
And write your password somewhere safe, but never share your password with strangers.
When my grandmother wanted to download a game, I downloaded it for her.
The game app is on her screen now.
Let me tell you my daily routine.
I charge my phone at night.
In the morning I look at the screen.
Then I open my weather app.
And then I download the news.
Then I check the screen for messages.
Then I open my cooking app.
Technology is part of life now.
We charge our phones, we download new things, we look at the screen, we open an app, and we type our password.
And every day we learn new English words.
Today our five words were charge, download, screen, app, and password.
See you tomorrow in the Word Kitchen.
